body: [A10] From both reviews of pull request #485 (issue 483): tb/verilator/pp_shadow mirrors the AUDIO_UNIT rate list of configs/endstation_arty_current.yaml by hand (AU_RATES_C); nothing fails if the configuration list changes and the bench copy does not. The hand-built image is the suite's deliberate design, so the fix belongs with this issue's builder-side bound: a gate that compares the bench constants with the configuration, or a generated header.

[A10] READINESS DECISION (2026-09-22)

Rechecked live dev b17580b91deb11f3441dfc5d7f9fafe539d929b8 and processor pin 424c688fa2205b934a7689a58f2aa766420f2326. Processor memory-map rule L10 still fixes the list at offset 144 and at most eight entries. `_load_clocking` still accepts excess/duplicate entries; the pp_shadow bench still spells AU_RATES_C independently.

Scope is settled: retain the list limit/duplicate refusals and gate 36a in the body. For the carried review finding, use a focused gate comparing the bench's AU_RATES_C values and declared length with configs/endstation_arty_current.yaml; keep the bench's deliberately hand-built image. Prove drift is refused and the pristine comparison passes. A generated header is unnecessary for this narrow contract. Preserve list order and all advertised shipping rates.

Authority: processor docs/architecture/07_memory_maps.md section 3.1 rule L10, REQUIREMENTS.md REQ-VER-03/04, and the issue's cited Milan 5.3.3.3. Acceptance additionally requires a legal eight-entry boundary case and a nine-entry refusal with distinct entries so duplicate rejection cannot mask the bound. Run the full builder gate, focused pp_shadow suite when its artifacts change, and the standard local/hosted/candidate/review bar. No donor code or shipping rate changes. No unresolved design decision remains.

Move to Ready; executor and two independent reviewers will be named before takeover. This is queued behind the active #407 author and the declaration bundle if its remaining decisions are settled in time.

[A156] IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS / FOCUSED EVIDENCE

Gate 36a checks the legal eight-entry boundary directly through `_load_clocking`, the contract named in acceptance. It uses eight distinct, deliberately unsorted values with the current rate last. This does not widen the downstream stream-format or runtime-rate contract. Negative cases use `load_config`; the ninth-entry fixture has nine distinct values, so duplicate rejection cannot supply its failure. Existing omitted-list defaults and current-rate membership are retained.

The pp_shadow drift gate lives in `sw/builder/test_builder.py`. It reads the existing literal `AU_RATES_C` declaration, checks its declared array length and ordered values against `configs/endstation_arty_current.yaml`, and rejects independent value, order, declared-length, shortened-initializer and commented-declaration controls. No pp_shadow source, Makefile or image is changed; no rate header is generated.

Focused gates 36a, 32 and 25a/b/c pass. Gate 36a failed on the original loader for accepting the distinct ninth entry. In-memory mutations raising the maximum to nine, lowering it to seven, and removing duplicate rejection each fail the focused test. All five config bytes and packed AEM images are SHA-256 identical to the pre-edit base b17580b91deb11f3441dfc5d7f9fafe539d929b8: arty_current advertises [48000, 96000, 192000]; the other four advertise [48000]. The complete builder run and xvlog are still in progress; broader manager gates are not claimed here.
